items.followUp: Explain the formation of an ionic bond in magnesium oxide (MgO).

rubric.why: The definition identifies electron transfer and the resulting oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic bond in terms of electron transfer and oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for electron transfer and 1 mark for the formation of oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: Sodium loses an electron to form a positive ion.
rubric.description: Explains the formation of the sodium ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sodium loses one electron to form Na+.

rubric.why: Chlorine gains an electron to form a negative ion.
rubric.description: Explains the formation of the chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorine gains an electron to form Cl−.

rubric.why: The example should identify the compound formed from the oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: Identifies sodium chloride as the ionic compound formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving NaCl as the product of the example.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another.
A sodium atom loses one electron to form a sodium ion: Na → Na+ + e−.
A chlorine atom gains this electron to form a chloride ion: Cl + e− → Cl−.
The oppositely charged Na+ and Cl− ions attract each other and form sodium chloride (NaCl).

items.followUp: Define rusting and explain how painting prevents it.

rubric.why: The definition should describe the gradual deterioration of a metal due to its surroundings.
rubric.description: Defines corrosion as the gradual destruction or deterioration of a metal through reaction with its environment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for gradual destruction or deterioration and 1 mark for identifying that a metal is affected.

rubric.why: Zinc coating, or galvanizing, is the specified method of protecting iron.
rubric.description: Identifies that iron is coated with zinc.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that iron is coated with zinc or galvanized.

rubric.why: The coating acts as a barrier between the iron and air and moisture.
rubric.description: Explains that zinc coating keeps air and moisture away from the iron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the barrier explanation.

rubric.why: Zinc corrodes preferentially and protects the iron, including when the coating is damaged.
rubric.description: Explains zinc's preferential corrosion and protection of iron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that zinc corrodes preferentially because it is more reactive than iron.

modelAnswer: Corrosion is the gradual destruction or deterioration of a metal due to its reaction with substances in the environment.
Iron can be protected by coating it with zinc; this process is called galvanizing.
The zinc layer prevents air and moisture from reaching the iron.
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes preferentially and protects the iron, even if the coating is scratched.

items.followUp: Define solubility and state three factors that affect it.

rubric.why: Solubility states the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a specified amount of solvent under stated conditions to form a saturated solution.
rubric.description: Defines solubility as the maximum amount of solute that dissolves to form a saturated solution under specified conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum-amount and saturated-solution definition with a stated condition or solvent amount.

rubric.why: The identities of the solute and solvent affect solubility.
rubric.description: Names the nature of the solute and solvent as a factor affecting solubility.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the nature of the solute and solvent.

rubric.description: Names temperature as a factor affecting solubility.

rubric.why: Pressure affects solubility, particularly for gases dissolved in liquids.
rubric.description: Names pressure as a factor affecting solubility.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature to form a saturated solution.
Three factors that affect solubility are the nature of the solute and solvent, temperature, and pressure (especially for gases).

items.followUp: Define a diatomic molecule and give one example.

rubric.why: Triatomic means that a molecule contains three atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a triatomic molecule by its number of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains three atoms.

rubric.why: A valid example must be a molecule containing three atoms.
rubric.description: Gives one correct example, such as H₂O, O₃, or CO₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: A triatomic molecule is a molecule that contains three atoms.
For example, a water molecule (H₂O) contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
